CGU1iqBpiBQ.title: The Values of Islam: Mas'uliyyah and Istikhlaf (Responsibility and Stewardship)
CGU1iqBpiBQ.one_line: Humans are stewards, not owners: with unique power comes answerability for oneself, family, community, creatures and the earth, and the opposite is indifference.
CGU1iqBpiBQ.summary: The sheikh pairs responsibility, which looks both back and forward, with stewardship, a forward-looking care that depends on it. Moral maturity, which we demand of children, means seeing what we hold as entrusted rather than owned, and adults forget to apply it to their homes, families and jobs. Humanity's place in the ecosystem is unique: unlike animals that adapt, humans reshape their environment, so power brings obligation and answerability, whether for climate change or for artificial intelligence, which needs stewards more than more intelligence. He grounds this in Allah appointing a khalifah on earth, Ibrahim made an imam, nations made successors to be tested, and the hadith that each of us is a shepherd who will be questioned. The hadith of planting a sapling as the Hour arrives shows that one does one's part however small. Responsibility starts with oneself but does not end there: Abu Bakr corrected those misusing the verse about minding oneself, and the ship parable shows we sail or sink together. Responsibility then widens with ability, from self to family, business and community. Its opposite is indifference. Dawud, who held nearly every human role, was the Quran's model khalifah, and Umar feared being asked about a stumbling animal. Children must be raised as caregivers.

outline.heading: Two values central to the prophets' message
outline.gist: Responsibility and stewardship may not hold the same centrality in other world religions.

outline.heading: Responsibility comes first
outline.gist: One can be responsible without being a steward, but stewardship cannot exist without responsibility.

outline.heading: Looking back and looking forward
outline.gist: Responsibility covers past acts and future duties, while stewardship looks forward; philosophers see both as the burden of being a self.

outline.heading: From mine to entrusted
outline.gist: We teach children that their toy is entrusted to them but forget that our homes, families and jobs are also trusts from Allah.

outline.heading: Power without stewardship
outline.gist: Power without responsibility is volatile; the world needs stewards of intelligence more than artificial intelligence.

outline.heading: What are we in the ecosystem?
outline.gist: Every creature fits its place; humans must ask whether they are members, masters or managers.

outline.heading: With power comes obligation
outline.gist: Free will and intelligence oblige humans to use their power responsibly.

outline.heading: Changing the environment and answering for it
outline.gist: Animals adapt over millions of years while humans reshape their surroundings, perhaps too much, and will be asked about it.

outline.heading: A khalifah on earth
outline.gist: Right after the opening of Al-Baqarah, Allah declares a steward on earth; earth, not Paradise, was always the plan.

outline.heading: Ibrahim made an imam
outline.gist: A steward is responsible for others' wellbeing on behalf of Someone else; what he holds is not his.

outline.heading: Successors so Allah sees how you act
outline.gist: Nations are made successors to be tested on what they do with their power.

outline.heading: Each of you is a shepherd
outline.gist: Ra'i means caregiver: the man at home, the woman in her house, the leader of his people, all will be questioned.

outline.heading: Plant the sapling as the Hour comes
outline.gist: Do your part however small, within the reach you have been given.

outline.heading: It starts with yourself, but does not end there
outline.gist: Some took the verse on minding oneself to mean no responsibility for others; Abu Bakr corrected that reading.

outline.heading: The ship: sail together or sink together
outline.gist: Those on the lower deck drilling a hole sink everyone unless others stop them.

outline.heading: We would rather not be responsible
outline.gist: People accept responsibility for themselves only to keep their freedom; Allah alone is not questioned, and this job description gives a Muslim his meaning.

outline.heading: The widening wingspan
outline.gist: Care grows from self to siblings, spouse, children, extended family, employees and community as Allah grants more.

outline.heading: The opposite is indifference
outline.gist: The first time the companions heard 'khalifah', they learned that 'not my problem' does not work.

outline.heading: Good and bad not caring
outline.gist: Not caring about people's opinions is admirable; not caring about moral responsibility is not.

outline.heading: Dawud, the model steward
outline.gist: Prophet, king, commander, craftsman, singer of the Zabur, judge, husband and father: he held the widest span of roles.

outline.heading: Caregivers of earth and creatures
outline.gist: Animals cannot make laws to avoid extinction; humans can protect them or destroy them and each other.

outline.heading: Umar and the stumbling animal
outline.gist: People in power today lack stewardship; Umar lay awake fearing he would be asked about an unpaved road.

outline.heading: Raising children as caregivers
outline.gist: Children must grow up knowing they are responsible for everything entrusted to them.

Ez7nRvCeL2U.title: The Values of Islam: Incorruptibility and Moral Absolutism (Istiqama)
Ez7nRvCeL2U.one_line: Istiqama means doing the right thing at every step regardless of outcomes: ends never justify means, and people are never means.
Ez7nRvCeL2U.summary: He explains that righteousness generates two ethics: justice, which concerns outcomes and people's rights, and istiqama, which concerns the journey and doing the right thing. Islam is not utilitarian. Muslims ask for the straight path at least seventeen times a day, a path rather than a destination, so the ends never justify the means. Even a magnificent goal like uniting the ummah or liberating Palestine cannot be pursued through corrupt steps; when Muslims copy enemies who kill children, nothing distinguishes them and they forfeit Allah's help, since victory is in His hands. The Prophet refused kingship and refused to seat the nobles of Quraysh apart from the poor, because that compromise would have corrupted the message. Values must be consistent across circumstances, otherwise they are preferences of convenience, and asking only what is right now makes decisions simpler. The truest karamah is steadfastness. Everyone knows, deep inside, what they could have done better in a conflict. Finally, people must never be used as means: the goal of Islam is guidance, not governance, so manipulating, exploiting or courting people for votes, and treating spouses or children as tools, is corruption. He asks listeners to judge every dilemma by people's rights and the right thing to do.

outline.heading: Values, principles and ethics recap
outline.gist: Values are what matter, principles are the actions, ethics decide between them; righteousness generates two core ethics.

outline.heading: Justice concerns outcomes; istiqama concerns the journey
outline.gist: Istiqama is best rendered as moral absolutism; Islam is not a utilitarian religion.

outline.heading: Guide us to the straight path: a path, not a destination
outline.gist: The daily prayer shows this is what Muslims care about most; morals are not bent by the goals pursued.

outline.heading: Why people corrupt their morals: the goals they chase
outline.gist: Istiqama does not even acknowledge an end; corruption begins when people want to get from A to B.

outline.heading: Every step must be as good as the goal
outline.gist: Even uniting the ummah or liberating Palestine cannot justify a single corrupt step.

outline.heading: Say I believe in Allah, then stand firm
outline.gist: The Prophet summed up everything in this short hadith; ends justifying means is a main source of corruption.

outline.heading: Corruption is the opposite of istiqama
outline.gist: Killing innocents, sowing fitnah or taking a little haram for a great cause makes you no different from your enemy and unworthy of Allah's help.

outline.heading: Outcomes belong to Allah
outline.gist: If the enemy plays dirty and gets ahead, so be it; they murder children and you do not, and that is the difference.

outline.heading: The only ethic we ask for daily
outline.gist: Al-Fatihah's other verses describe Allah; the one request for ourselves is guidance to the straight path.

outline.heading: The Prophet refused corrupt shortcuts
outline.gist: He turned down kingship and the nobles' demand to be taught apart from the poor, since that would compromise equality.

outline.heading: Ethical consistency
outline.gist: A value that changes with circumstances is a preference of convenience; the generous are generous rich or poor.

outline.heading: Ask only what is right now
outline.gist: Strategizing about outcomes clouds choices; doing the right thing costs relationships but makes decisions simple.

outline.heading: Istiqama as the greatest karamah
outline.gist: Physical wonders can happen to anyone; steadfastness on the straight path is the gift given to those closest to Allah.

outline.heading: Ends never justify means: undebatable
outline.gist: Ethical dilemmas exist and need study, but the principle itself is not open to debate.

outline.heading: Everyone knows what they could have done differently
outline.gist: In any conflict ask what you could have done better; ethics are personal regardless of what others did.

outline.heading: People are never means
outline.gist: Islam's goal is guidance, not governance; manipulating, lying to or exploiting people takes away their free will.

outline.heading: In teaching, the student is the goal
outline.gist: If he taught to gain loyal volunteers, he would be corrupt; the aim is the listener's own success.

outline.heading: Politicians who treat voters as means
outline.gist: They court you until you vote and then vanish, yet people accept it; speak on principle instead.

outline.heading: Spouses and children are not means
outline.gist: A spouse's dreams and dignity matter, and children are not tools for a parent's name or glory.

outline.heading: Judging every dilemma by rights and the right thing
outline.gist: Return to people's rights and what is right; deep down everyone knows, and we ask Allah to guide us to it.

0sIP1s48hx8.title: The Values of Islam: Wasatiyyah (Balance and Moderation)
0sIP1s48hx8.one_line: Wasatiyyah is not a middle point but the method for applying Islam's values: anti-extremism, calibrated intensity, embracing opposites, guarding against bid'ah, keeping life functional.
0sIP1s48hx8.summary: In this Ramadan episode of his values series, the sheikh places wasatiyyah right after the three judging ethics of truth, justice and moral absolutism, arguing it is not itself an ethic but the method by which every ethic is applied. Drawing on the description of the ummah as a middle nation, the verses on the scale (mizan) and on balanced spending, he explains that wasat in Arabic means the best-proportioned, not the average. He develops it across four domains. First, it opposes extremism, not absolutism: we hold firm truths but carry them with empathy. Second, it is calibrated intensity in emotion, against swinging between adoring and condemning people. Third, it is the embrace of apparent opposites, such as tawakkul and effort, firm identity and tolerance, equality and difference between men and women, being both servant and steward. Fourth, it protects the deen from bid'ah, illustrated by the three men who wanted to outdo the Prophet's worship and by Christian celibacy, which broke human functionality. He insists balance only operates after full certainty in faith, warns lay people against throwing the word bid'ah around, and says every later value in the series, from courage to selflessness, will be practised through moderation.

outline.heading: Values judged by three ethics
outline.gist: He places this topic right after truth, justice and moral absolutism, the three standards by which every choice in the deen is judged.

outline.heading: Value, virtue or method?
outline.gist: Scholars disagree on how to classify wasatiyyah; he argues it cannot judge a dilemma and is instead the method of applying ethics.

outline.heading: A nation made middle to be witnesses
outline.gist: The ummah is described as balanced so that humanity can see how a balanced life is lived.

outline.heading: The scale built into creation
outline.gist: Allah created everything with a delicate balance and forbids ruining it; balance means proportionality, not blandness.

outline.heading: Spending: neither tight-fisted nor open-handed
outline.gist: The Quranic examples of giving show the balanced zone between stinginess and leaving oneself with nothing.

outline.heading: What wasat means in Arabic
outline.gist: A wasat mountain is the best-proportioned one, with just enough of everything, not the one in the middle.

outline.heading: Domain one: opposite of extremism, not of absolutism
outline.gist: Truth is not averaged between positions; moderation governs how we hold and convey firm truths, with empathy and understanding.

outline.heading: Domain two: calibrated intensity
outline.gist: People swing from adoring a scholar to condemning him over one remark; responses should be proportionate.

outline.heading: Love and dislike in moderation
outline.gist: A narration urges moderate love and hate; he extends it to balancing material and spiritual life, form and essence, hope and fear.

outline.heading: Domain three: embracing opposites, tawakkul and effort
outline.gist: Full reliance on Allah and full planning coexist; understanding why both are needed is cracking the code of Islam.

outline.heading: Firm identity with tolerance
outline.gist: Muslims compromise nothing of who they are yet respect the autonomy of those who disagree and live peacefully with them.

outline.heading: Men and women: equal and different
outline.gist: Both statements hold at once; roles, needs and experiences differ while worth is equal.

outline.heading: Servant and steward at once
outline.gist: Dropping either side of the human role breaks the balance and the purpose of creation.

outline.heading: Domain four: protection from bid'ah, the three men
outline.gist: The usul scholars call wasatiyyah the wall against bid'ah; the Prophet rebuked the men who vowed never to sleep, marry or break fast.

outline.heading: Balance comes after certainty
outline.gist: Wasatiyyah is not a foot in each camp; it operates only once faith is held with full certainty.

outline.heading: Moderation in other traditions
outline.gist: Aristotle, early Christianity and Buddhism valued moderation, but Allah chose it as the defining description of this ummah.

outline.heading: An ummah of right proportions
outline.gist: Care for body and spirit, individual and community, worship and enjoyment of life, all at once.

outline.heading: Bid'ah in the Prophet's time was extremism
outline.gist: Innovation then appeared as people breaking the proportions of practice.

outline.heading: Bid'ah is a word for scholars
outline.gist: It is not one of the five rulings but an alarm that the boundaries of Islam are breached, so students should not use it casually.

outline.heading: The man fasting in the sun
outline.gist: The Prophet let him keep his fast but told him to sit and seek shade, dropping the invented additions.

outline.heading: Moderation keeps life functional
outline.gist: Filling only one of three buckets makes you walk crooked; everything needs proportionate care.

outline.heading: Celibacy: the Quran's one example of bid'ah
outline.gist: Monasticism was invented and never prescribed; denying a basic human need ruined functionality.

outline.heading: Marriage as the balanced answer
outline.gist: Neither deprivation nor overindulgence; both extremes lead to lasting harm.

outline.heading: Piety does not mean deprivation
outline.gist: A pious person marries, eats well and vacations with family; even prayer volume should be between loud and silent.

outline.heading: Recap of the four domains
outline.gist: Within certainty, move forward without extremism, with calibrated intensity, embracing opposites, and protected from deviation.

outline.heading: The only 'how' of the series
outline.gist: Every other value is a 'what'; courage, for example, sits between cowardice and recklessness.

outline.heading: Selflessness in moderation
outline.gist: Be selfless but leave something for your family, so they are not left with nothing.

3:143.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ تَمَنَّوۡنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَلۡقَوۡهُ فَقَدۡ رَأَيۡتُمُوهُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
3:143.en: And you had certainly wished for martyrdom before you encountered it, and you have [now] seen it [before you] while you were looking on

3:144.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُۚ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَسَيَجۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:144.en: Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And he who turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful

3:145.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفۡسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبࣰ ا مُّؤَجَّلࣰ اۗ وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَاۚ وَسَنَجۡزِي ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
3:145.en: And it is not [possible] for one to die except by permission of Allah at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him thereof. And we will reward the grateful

3:154.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةࣰ نُّعَاسࣰ ا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةࣰ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةࣱ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءࣱ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
3:154.en: Then after distress, He sent down upon you security [in the form of] drowsiness, overcoming a faction of you, while another faction worried about themselves, thinking of Allah other than the truth - the thought of ignorance, saying, "Is there anything for us [to have done] in this matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter belongs completely to Allah." They conceal within themselves what they will not reveal to you. They say, "If there was anything we could have done in the matter, some of us would not have been killed right here." Say, "Even if you had been inside your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their death beds." [It was] so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts

3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and we bring you, [O Muhammad] against these [people] as a witness

7:34.ar: وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلࣱۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةࣰ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ
7:34.en: And for every nation is a [specified] term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal

hTmH_0H4oLE.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 4: Quranic Themes 2 - Accepting Mortality
hTmH_0H4oLE.one_line: Making peace with death through Uhud's lessons in Aal-Imran, 'every soul shall taste death', and the Prophet weeping at Ibn Mas'ud's recitation.
hTmH_0H4oLE.summary: He argues that even practising Muslims have lost a basic part of the faith: being at peace with the fact that life can end at any moment. Endings give life its meaning, so children should learn about death as soon as they can understand it, and they learn to take life for granted from parents who do; without this acceptance a loss becomes a breaking point rather than a lesson. Reading the Uhud verses, he shows companions who had wished for martyrdom faltering when a rumour spread that the Prophet had fallen. The Quran reminds them that Muhammad is a messenger like those before him, that faith cannot rest on any leader, teacher or hero, and that no soul dies except at its appointed time, which should produce courage rather than compromise. From 'every soul shall taste death' he urges people to cherish youth, health, company and Ramadan while they have them, to see worldly pleasures as short-lived highs, and to judge every pursuit by whether it moves them away from the Fire and into Paradise. He closes with the Prophet stopping Ibn Mas'ud's recitation in tears at the verse about bringing him as witness over his nation.

outline.heading: Accepting mortality: inner peace with an ending
outline.gist: Being at peace with not living forever is common to nearly all religions and fades as people drift from faith.

outline.heading: Practising Muslims have drifted from it too
outline.gist: Even people who read a lot of Quran and practise diligently have lost their acceptance that life can end at any moment.

outline.heading: The Quran's guidance assumes we are mortal
outline.gist: Every teaching in the Quran is built on the fact that people and nations pass; existence without an end would not be existence.

outline.heading: Endings give life meaning
outline.gist: A football game that never ended would mean nothing; purpose, meaning and morality exist because life ends.

outline.heading: Teaching children about death
outline.gist: Present death as early as children can grasp it, as with his four-year-old son, so they value being alive rather than to frighten them.

outline.heading: Children take life for granted when parents do
outline.gist: Children who take their blessings for granted learned that life is a given from parents who never feel they have enough.

outline.heading: Without acceptance, loss becomes a breaking point
outline.gist: An unexpected death breaks people's faith and sense of purpose instead of prompting reflection, which is why the Quran mentions death so often.

outline.heading: Aal-Imran and the shock of Uhud
outline.gist: The second half of the surah addresses internal threats to faith; Uhud shook the community and made some question the message.

outline.heading: You used to wish for death
outline.gist: Some had spoken eagerly of martyrdom; the Prophet taught never to wish to meet the enemy but to ask Allah for wellbeing and stand firm if it comes.

outline.heading: Seeing death changes everything
outline.gist: Intentions are easy in conversation; on the battlefield, seeing blood and hearing that the Prophet had fallen, perspective changed.

outline.heading: Mus'ab falls and the rumour spreads
outline.gist: Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who resembled the Prophet, was killed holding the banner, and the rumour of the Prophet's death caused chaos and flight.

outline.heading: Muhammad is only a messenger
outline.gist: Messengers passed before him; Allah never granted any human immortality, so would they turn on their heels if he died?

outline.heading: Islam is a gift; Allah rewards the grateful
outline.gist: Those who turn back harm only themselves; standing for something pure is a gift most people never receive.

outline.heading: No soul dies except at its appointed term
outline.gist: Your time was set before birth, which should comfort rather than fill you with regret; the term is hidden until it arrives.

outline.heading: Faith cannot rest on a leader
outline.gist: Your deen must stand on what you know to be true, whether or not the Prophet, your teacher, or political heroes remain.

outline.heading: When it's time, it's time
outline.gist: In hospital some who should have died live on and others fall without explanation; no doctor or technology can delay a decreed death.

outline.heading: Even at home, the decreed would meet their end
outline.gist: Knowing death cannot be outrun gives courage and inner peace, so a believer holds his ground instead of selling out his values.

outline.heading: Every soul shall taste death
outline.gist: The verse recited at every funeral states a fact decreed from the moment each soul was created.

outline.heading: Every organ has an expiry date
outline.gist: Even escaping all illness, the brain, eyes and every organ will eventually stop working.

outline.heading: Cherish youth and health while you have them
outline.gist: The body is a trust to care for; enjoy working joints and a quick memory now, because they decline.

outline.heading: You ain't dead yet
outline.gist: Every decade envies the one before; we are already tasting death, which should lift the mood because we are still alive.

outline.heading: Don't take life for granted
outline.gist: Enjoy every breath, the people around you and this blessed night; stepping back from taking life for granted makes everything under it precious.

outline.heading: Moved away from the Fire: the only victory
outline.gist: Full recompense comes on Judgment Day; whoever is edged away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has won.

outline.heading: 'It is only your deeds'
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi Allah says He records people's deeds and returns them; whoever finds otherwise can blame only himself.

outline.heading: People and Ramadans: limited time only
outline.gist: Every person is interesting and precious, but our time with them and our Ramadans are limited, so enjoy them now.

outline.heading: Worldly life: short-lived highs
outline.gist: Worldly pleasures are illusions that seem bigger than they are, like the finest meal that sickens a full stomach.

outline.heading: Measure everything by the one win
outline.gist: Study, work and family should all move you toward Paradise; anything that does not deserves rethinking.

outline.heading: The Prophet asks Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him
outline.gist: For the first time the Prophet asked a companion, one of the greatest scholars of the Sahabah, to recite the Quran to him.

outline.heading: A student in the zone
outline.gist: Ibn Mas'ud recited close and fully absorbed, a state he describes from his own joy as a Quran teacher watching students recite.

outline.heading: 'Enough': a witness over his nation
outline.gist: At the verse about bringing a witness from every nation, the Prophet stopped him in tears, thinking of his own death and accounting.

36:12.ar: إِنَّا نَحۡنُ نُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُواْ وَءَاثَٰرَهُمۡۚ وَكُلَّ شَيۡءٍ أَحۡصَيۡنَٰهُ فِيٓ إِمَامࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏

36:14.ar: إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡهِمُ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزۡنَا بِثَالِثࣲ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُم مُّرۡسَلُونَ

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ

36:17.en: And we are not responsible except for clear notification

36:18.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرۡنَا بِكُمۡۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرۡجُمَنَّكُمۡ وَلَيَمَسَّنَّكُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
36:18.en: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment

36:19.ar: قَالُواْ طَٰٓئِرُكُم مَّعَكُمۡ أَئِن ذُكِّرۡتُمۚ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ مُّسۡرِفُونَ

B218EFMby-M.title: Tafseer of Surat Yasin, Part 2 (13-19)
B218EFMby-M.one_line: Indifference as a choice, then the people of the township: messengers rejected out of ego, suspicion of selfless work, and superstition.
B218EFMby-M.summary: He recaps the opening verses: the opposite of a living heart is indifference, normal in youth but a choice in adulthood. The decree that most will not believe follows their own choices, and he separates forgetting from neglect, which even a court recognizes. He pleads with people not to wait until they lose something to value it, and explains why he named the Imam Development Academy after the Quranic sense of imam as a role model whose legacy is followed. He then gives his historical reading of the story of the township: the Antioch region in the Greek-Iranian period under a king who claimed divine lineage and then vanished from the records, which fits the Quranic pattern of peoples who disappear. Through the verses he explains qaryah as a mixed population, the general word for those sent, and the rare sending of two messengers reinforced by a third. The rejection, you are only humans like us, shows that most great conflicts come down to petty ego, as with Abu Jahl's envy. People cannot believe work with no catch, so Muslims must keep their own service free of hidden strings. Finally he dissects superstition: the township blamed the messengers as bad omens, just as communities today blame jinn and the evil eye to avoid facing mental illness and their own failures.

outline.heading: The opposite of a living heart is indifference
outline.gist: He recaps that true life is the life of the heart and its opposite is a life of indifference to what you have been given.

outline.heading: Indifference in youth and the turn to adulthood
outline.gist: Children cannot be expected to zoom out; by adulthood people must, and religion makes the meaning clear though anyone can find it.

outline.heading: Rituals kept as empty skeletons
outline.gist: Muslims manage to fast and pray while living oblivious lives, keeping the acts without their essence, and they feel the emptiness.

outline.heading: The oath and the mission restated
outline.gist: The Prophet does not speak from himself; he was sent with a message that puts people on a clear, straight path.

outline.heading: The word has come true upon most: decree follows choice
outline.gist: When Allah decrees that someone will not find guidance, it is always based on a choice they made, never arbitrary dislike.

outline.heading: Forgetfulness versus neglect
outline.gist: Forgetting once is human; being reminded again and again and still ignoring it is neglect, and indifference is a choice.

outline.heading: Shackles and those who follow the reminder
outline.gist: He revisits the shackled people who look upward and the receptive person who does not want to live oblivious.

outline.heading: Do not wait until you lose something
outline.gist: People wake up only when they lose someone or something precious; the remorse is painful, so cherish it now.

outline.heading: Good tidings and giving life to the dead
outline.gist: Those with reverence for the unseen receive good news, and Allah records what people did and what followed from it.

outline.heading: Imam as a role model: naming the Imam Development Academy
outline.gist: He chose the name despite pushback because imam in the Quran means an exemplar like Ibrahim whose legacy others follow.

outline.heading: The township story: dating it and the apostles view
outline.gist: He dates it about a century before Isa and rejects the view that the messengers were the apostles of Isa.

outline.heading: Antioch, the Greek-Iranian period and Mount Nemrut
outline.gist: He places the story in the Antioch region under a king who claimed divine lineage and built a great temple on Mount Nemrut.

outline.heading: A king who vanishes from the historical record
outline.gist: Historians cannot say what happened to the king; he reads the sudden end as fitting the Quranic account of punished peoples.

outline.heading: Rock-carved cities with no records
outline.gist: The ruins in Arabia of people who carved castles into rock and then left no trace tell the same story the Quran tells.

outline.heading: Strike for them an example
outline.gist: The verse opens the story as an example to be set before the people.

outline.heading: Qaryah: a town of mixed peoples
outline.gist: Citing a Quranic geographical atlas, he says qaryah denotes a population of different backgrounds, fitting the Greek-Iranian setting.

outline.heading: Rasul, nabi and the general word for those sent
outline.gist: Messengers bring new law and prophets do not; the word used here only says they were sent, without specifying which.

outline.heading: Two messengers sent at once
outline.gist: Two messengers to one people is rare in the Quran, the nearest examples being Yahya with Isa and Musa with Harun.

outline.heading: Reinforced by a third: unity among messengers
outline.gist: The third messenger strengthened the others; each had his own signs yet they agreed with one another.

outline.heading: You are only humans like us
outline.gist: People resent being called by someone like them who was chosen for something they were not.

outline.heading: The world's big problems come down to petty ego
outline.gist: Wars and conflicts trace back to an unchecked disease of the heart, as Pharaoh's saga came from one insecure man's arrogance.

outline.heading: Why messengers are human: the test of the ego
outline.gist: Had angels been sent they would have come as men, because the test is whether you can get over yourself and listen.

outline.heading: Abu Jahl's envy
outline.gist: Abu Jahl privately admitted the Prophet was truthful but would not follow him because his rival clan now had a prophet.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah as getting over the self; the Prophet had no ego
outline.gist: Every conflict comes down to something we are too stubborn to get over; the Prophet would give up his ego whenever it solved a problem.

outline.heading: Our only duty is to convey clearly
outline.gist: The messengers answer that Allah knows they were sent and their only obligation is clear conveyance, not control.

outline.heading: People cannot believe there is no catch
outline.gist: Those ruled by ego assume everyone has a hidden motive; real Islamic work seeks its return only after death.

outline.heading: If there are strings attached, say so upfront
outline.gist: Service with hidden expectations is not for Allah; the Prophet's only condition in the pledge was lifelong commitment to the cause.

outline.heading: You are a bad omen to us: superstition as the go-to discredit
outline.gist: Unable to accuse the messengers of anything, the people blamed them for bad luck.

outline.heading: Superstition rises with ignorance; Islam removed it
outline.gist: Superstition correlates inversely with education; the Prophet removed practices like the divining arrows the Arabs carried.

outline.heading: Blaming the evil eye for everything
outline.gist: In his village every misfortune, from not marrying to cancer after decades of smoking, was blamed on envy and the eye.

outline.heading: Not wanting to rock the boat
outline.gist: The message threatened the king and the status quo, and people avoid controversy even when the whole system is built on lies.

outline.heading: Threats of stoning and your omen is within you
outline.gist: The messengers reply that the omen lies with the people themselves, who go beyond all limits when they dislike a message.

outline.heading: Superstition masks mental illness; why we know about envy
outline.gist: Knowing the evil eye exists is meant to make us humble and careful, not to explain results that have clear causes.

outline.heading: Blaming jinn to avoid facing ourselves
outline.gist: It is easier to blame a jinn than admit a family member's anxiety and depression went unnoticed; superstition is what people reach for when they have no argument.

im7_zZK6pnE.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 8: Quranic Themes 2 - Demise of the Vain
im7_zZK6pnE.one_line: How vanity clouds judgment and destroys people, read through Adam's deception, Thamud's arrogant leaders and Allah withholding His signs from the arrogant.
im7_zZK6pnE.summary: He defines the vain as those who overestimate themselves and their deeds, and argues that once vanity takes hold every later judgment is built on a false starting point. The cure is an accurate view: every human has a fixed divine value that no status can raise and no humiliation can lower, which is why slavery and racism are false, but our efforts really are flawed and mediocre, and admitting that is the only path to growth. Valuing our own deeds trespasses on Allah's role as their judge. In Al-A'raf, Shaytan swore he was a sincere adviser and led Adam and Hawwa like a carrot, exploiting the vanity that bristled at being mortal servants; the exposure of their nakedness is read by scholars as their moral flaws coming to light. They had been warned, which shows that knowing what is right is not enough if an inner weakness remains, so we must trace why we fell and seal the crack. Thamud's arrogant leaders rejected Salih simply because the weak believed in him, then killed the she-camel; the Quraysh likewise demanded separate sessions for nobles. He closes with Allah's statement that He turns the arrogant away from His signs.

outline.heading: The vain: overvaluing oneself and one's deeds
outline.gist: A theme found almost everywhere in the Quran; he returns to vanity and arrogance in every series because the Quran does.

outline.heading: Vanity destroys judgment
outline.gist: An inflated sense of self makes every later assessment false because it rests on a false first premise.

outline.heading: Neither more nor less than a servant
outline.gist: Humans have real divine value but are servants of Allah; the pendulum swinging either way causes trouble.

outline.heading: Divine value versus potential
outline.gist: We come from soil, are flawed and ignorant by nature with great potential; our human value stays the same whether emperor or paraded in disgrace.

outline.heading: Why slavery and racism are false
outline.gist: They claim some people have less human value by nature, which is simply untrue.

outline.heading: Humility is not a lie you tell yourself
outline.gist: Pretending to be less good while believing otherwise masks vanity; the truth is our efforts are flawed, and admitting it is the only way to grow.

outline.heading: Vanity as a pathology
outline.gist: Successful, wealthy, popular people often end up miserable and self-destructive; vanity is a spiritual and psychological disease that brings its own ruin.

outline.heading: Only Allah appraises our deeds
outline.gist: We compete in taqwa and hope Allah values our actions; declaring our own deeds praiseworthy oversteps into His domain.

outline.heading: Shaytan swore he was a sincere adviser
outline.gist: Adam's story recurs across the Quran with deliberate differences; here Shaytan leads them on with what they wanted, like a carrot.

outline.heading: Exploiting the weakness within
outline.gist: Shaytan used no outside force but their inner vanity; the story is the raw human experience, a solved problem for us, not a slight on Adam.

outline.heading: Servant does not sound attractive
outline.gist: Told they were mortal servants, the nafs struck back insisting it was a king, and Shaytan promised them a higher rank.

outline.heading: Led on by delusion
outline.gist: The person full of himself has clouded judgment; their vanity became a barrier that kept them from seeing how they were being played.

outline.heading: Nakedness as exposed flaws
outline.gist: Scholars read the exposure figuratively: their vanity and fear came to light, as shameful as being naked, and covering with leaves of Paradise means its teachings.

outline.heading: They had already been warned
outline.gist: Allah had told them the tree was forbidden and Shaytan their enemy; he once studied the story for weeks assuming they did not know.

outline.heading: Knowing the right thing is not enough
outline.gist: If a weakness remains inside, Shaytan exploits it and you later cannot believe what you did.

outline.heading: Find out why you did it, then seal the crack
outline.gist: Rather than burying a shameful episode, work out exactly what was exploited so it cannot be used again; vanity is a carrot chased for life.

outline.heading: Al-A'raf: succeeding as a community
outline.gist: The surah's prophet stories stress communal worship and success; we cannot afford indifference because we sail or sink together.

outline.heading: Thamud: rich, spoiled and indifferent
outline.gist: Salih's people had great wealth and power and took it for granted when he came to correct them.

outline.heading: The town hall: 'we reject whatever you believe'

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ

9:118.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلَٰثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا ضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَن لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّآ إِلَيۡهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لِيَتُوبُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

6SmV1nBWrEo.title: The Values of Islam: Sidq (Honesty) and Amanah (Trustworthiness)
6SmV1nBWrEo.one_line: Honesty is absolute and begins with honesty toward oneself; trustworthiness is honesty plus guarding others' rights, and without both no person or society survives.
6SmV1nBWrEo.summary: The sheikh opens by arguing that Islamic revival means reviving its values, which have never changed from Adam to Muhammad, and that masjids should send children home knowing what they stand for. He then takes honesty and trustworthiness, defined through their opposites, lying and betrayal. Honesty is absolute apart from narrow exceptions such as compliments, war and reconciling people. It starts with self-honesty: a person who lies to himself ends up sincerely telling lies, like those who will swear falsely to Allah on the Day of Judgment. Ka'b ibn Malik's truthfulness after Tabuk shows that honesty earns no reward and may bring hard consequences, yet lies always snap back and multiply into a web. Trustworthiness is honesty combined with preserving others' rights; it takes years to build and one breach to destroy. The Prophet's role at the Black Stone dispute, his challenge at Safa and Ali returning the deposits of his persecutors show his trust. Hypocrisy is the opposite of both. He urges parents to break children's early discovery that lying solves problems, notes that honesty is the door to tawbah, and shows that money, neighbourhoods and the greeting of salam all rest on trust.

outline.heading: Values are what reviving Islam means
outline.gist: Revival is not governance or politics but the ethics Islam came to instill, unchanged from Adam to Muhammad.

outline.heading: What masjids should teach children
outline.gist: The series' framework is for passing on to children, who should leave the masjid clear on their values.

outline.heading: Values known by their opposites
outline.gist: He orders values by importance and introduces honesty and trust through their opposites, lying and betrayal.

outline.heading: Honesty as the most basic value
outline.gist: Some scholars see honesty as the most important value or the one never to be breached.

outline.heading: The narrow exceptions
outline.gist: Compliments, war and reconciling estranged people are not counted as lying; outside them there is no excuse.

outline.heading: Honesty starts with yourself
outline.gist: Lying to yourself means later telling lies you believe, a distortion fixable only by going back to the first lie.

outline.heading: Those who swear falsely to Allah
outline.gist: People will swear on Judgment Day as they swore in this life, believing their own lie; they are the true liars.

outline.heading: Ka'b ibn Malik after Tabuk
outline.gist: He alone with two others admitted he had no excuse and then endured fifty days of boycott.

outline.heading: Honesty is not owed a reward
outline.gist: Expect consequences for admitting a mistake; distorting reality snaps back harder in this life or the next.

outline.heading: The web of lies
outline.gist: One lie needs another to defend it until a person no longer knows what is real; the young should never start.

outline.heading: Honesty forces better choices
outline.gist: Bad choices create the need to lie; committing to honesty pushes you to behave better.

outline.heading: Trust is honesty plus guarding rights
outline.gist: Trust builds over years into a reputation, and one breach ends it.

outline.heading: The Black Stone dispute
outline.gist: The tribes accepted the Prophet's judgment because amanah is how honesty shows itself: one face, one narrative.

outline.heading: Hypocrisy as the opposite
outline.gist: The signs of the hypocrite, lying and betraying, are the reverse of these two values.

outline.heading: Al-Amin of Makkah and the call at Safa
outline.gist: People left their valuables with him and admitted they had never known him to lie in forty years.

outline.heading: Returning the trusts of his persecutors
outline.gist: He left Ali behind to return deposits to the people who tried to kill him; institutions today struggle to earn such trust.

outline.heading: Children discover that lying works
outline.gist: Parents and the community must teach early that lies that solve problems now rot one's ethics.

outline.heading: Truth leads to righteousness
outline.gist: Honesty leads to every virtue and to Paradise; lying leads to fujur, a life without a moral compass.

outline.heading: A believer may slip but will not lie
outline.gist: Admitting what you did is the only path to tawbah and redemption.

outline.heading: Lying to Allah, to yourself, to people
outline.gist: Lying to people is the least of the three and a consequence of the other two lies already told.

outline.heading: Society is built on trust
outline.gist: Money, politics and letting a child walk to school all depend on trust; pre-Islamic Arabia lived without it.

outline.heading: Salam as a declaration of safety
outline.gist: Strangers in the desert met in a showdown until the Prophet introduced a greeting that promises safety.

outline.heading: The untrusted live alone
outline.gist: People who cannot find work, marriage or friends often do not see that others have identified them as dishonest.

outline.heading: The hallmarks of the Prophet's followers
outline.gist: He was the truthful and trustworthy one; without these there is little else to discuss.

5:33.ar: إِنَّمَا جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَيَسۡعَوۡنَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَسَادًا أَن يُقَتَّلُوٓاْ أَوۡ يُصَلَّبُوٓاْ أَوۡ تُقَطَّعَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَأَرۡجُلُهُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفٍ أَوۡ يُنفَوۡاْ مِنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ ذَٰلِكَ لَهُمۡ خِزۡيࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَلَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
5:33.en: Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment

5:34.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَقۡدِرُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
5:34.en: Except for those who return [repenting] before you apprehend them. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

5:78.ar: لُعِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ عَلَىٰ لِسَانِ دَاوُۥدَ وَعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
5:78.en: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed

5:79.ar: كَانُواْ لَا يَتَنَاهَوۡنَ عَن مُّنكَرࣲ فَعَلُوهُۚ لَبِئۡسَ مَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
5:79.en: They used not to prevent one another from wrongdoing that they did. How wretched was that which they were doing

5:106.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ شَهَٰدَةُ بَيۡنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ حِينَ ٱلۡوَصِيَّةِ ٱثۡنَانِ ذَوَا عَدۡلࣲ مِّنكُمۡ أَوۡ ءَاخَرَانِ مِنۡ غَيۡرِكُمۡ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ ضَرَبۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَأَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۚ تَحۡبِسُونَهُمَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ فَيُقۡسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ إِنِ ٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ لَا نَشۡتَرِي بِهِۦ ثَمَنࣰ ا وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰ وَلَا نَكۡتُمُ شَهَٰدَةَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلۡأٓثِمِينَ
5:106.en: O you who have believed, testimony [should be taken] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest - [that of] two just men from among you or two others from outside if you are traveling through the land and the disaster of death should strike you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you doubt [their testimony, saying], "We will not exchange our oath for a price, even if he should be a near relative, and we will not withhold the testimony of Allah. Indeed, we would then be of the sinful

5:107.ar: فَإِنۡ عُثِرَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنَّهُمَا ٱسۡتَحَقَّآ إِثۡمࣰ ا فَـَٔاخَرَانِ يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَحَقَّ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡأَوۡلَيَٰنِ فَيُقۡسِمَانِ بِٱللَّهِ لَشَهَٰدَتُنَآ أَحَقُّ مِن شَهَٰدَتِهِمَا وَمَا ٱعۡتَدَيۡنَآ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
5:107.en: But if it is found that those two were guilty of perjury, let two others stand in their place [who are] foremost [in claim] from those who have a lawful right. And let them swear by Allah, "Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed. Indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers

5:108.ar: ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يَأۡتُواْ بِٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهَآ أَوۡ يَخَافُوٓاْ أَن تُرَدَّ أَيۡمَٰنُۢ بَعۡدَ أَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسۡمَعُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:108.en: That is more likely that they will give testimony according to its [true] objective, or [at least] they would fear that [other] oaths might be taken after their oaths. And fear Allah and listen; and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people

24:2.ar: ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجۡلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا مِاْئَةَ جَلۡدَةࣲۖ وَلَا تَأۡخُذۡكُم بِهِمَا رَأۡفَةࣱ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۖ وَلۡيَشۡهَدۡ عَذَابَهُمَا طَآئِفَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
24:2.en: The [unmarried] woman or [unmarried] man found guilty of sexual intercourse - lash each one of them with a hundred lashes, and do not be taken by pity for them in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment

5:38.ar: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
5:38.en: [As for] the thief, the male and the female, amputate their hands in recompense for what they committed as a deterrent [punishment] from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

24:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةࣰ وَلَا تَقۡبَلُواْ لَهُمۡ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدࣰ اۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:4.en: And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - lash them with eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient

egCfkHpXGo8.speaker_note: Sheikh Adnan's Ramadan Quranic Themes series; speaks of his emergency medicine training and growing up in Syria
egCfkHpXGo8.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 6: Quranic Themes 2 - Protecting Public Interest
egCfkHpXGo8.one_line: Al-Ma'idah on protecting the collective: the hirabah penalty, the duty to object to wrong, and trustworthy testimony as the basis of hadith.
egCfkHpXGo8.summary: He places Al-Ma'idah in the story of the seven long surahs as the book of covenants, whose commands protect not only the individual's faith, life, wealth, mind and honour but the public as a whole. The West, he argues, has traded public interest for individual freedom, as the pandemic and the endless overdose cycles he saw in emergency medicine show, while good parents restrict children's freedoms out of love. The hirabah verse, the strictest in the Quran, targets those who wage war on society and spread corruption: organized crime, drug networks and rape, which destroy people's safety in their homes, as he saw happen to Syria, and leave neglected youth with no future, a failure he lays partly on the community. The same logic explains why public zina is punished and private sin is left to Allah, and the door of repentance shows the aim is protection, not brutality. The second passage condemns the Children of Israel for staying silent about wrongdoing among them; a community survives only if people gently but firmly object. The last passage sets rules for witnesses to a deathbed bequest, which later became the foundation for judging hadith narrators. He asks people to care about the collective, speak up against wrong and be trustworthy in what they convey.

outline.heading: Public interest as a main purpose of Islam
outline.gist: Protecting the public is one of the central aims of the deen, and Al-Ma'idah has a clear place in the story told by the seven long surahs.

outline.heading: Al-Ma'idah: the covenants and commands
outline.gist: After the job description, its protection and the ethical system, Al-Ma'idah gives the dos and don'ts in roughly fifteen commands addressed to the believers, each followed by commentary.

outline.heading: Protecting the individual
outline.gist: Islam clearly protects each person's freedom of belief, life, wealth, intellect and reputation.

outline.heading: Protecting the collective, and the West's blind spot
outline.gist: Islam also protects the group, while the West has watered this down by putting individual freedom above the public's interest.

outline.heading: The hudud make sense only through public interest
outline.gist: Severe penalties for murder, theft after break-in, public zina and false accusation look like attacks on dignity until you see what they protect.

outline.heading: The pandemic lesson about personal freedom
outline.gist: Until 2019 eating anything was a private freedom, then a single meal made the world sick; some choices threaten everyone and need limits.

outline.heading: Frequent flyers in the emergency department
outline.gist: Patients who overdose every few nights cost the public system, yet suggesting limits on their freedom becomes a political smear.

outline.heading: Restricting freedom as an act of mercy
outline.gist: Loving parents restrict their children's freedom so they can later live well; Allah addresses humanity in a similar way, at a far higher level.

outline.heading: Terror and the value of feeling safe at home
outline.gist: The verse targets those who spread terror; once people stop feeling safe in their homes, a chain of consequences follows.

outline.heading: Open doors in Syria, then lost forever
outline.gist: He grew up sleeping with the doors open and driving to Damascus at night; once that safety was lost, people's ethics and openness changed with it.

outline.heading: Waging war on society: the strictest verse
outline.gist: Those who provoke war and organize ongoing corruption, like racketeering networks of theft, killing and drugs, ruin countries and generations.

outline.heading: No one sits neutral
outline.gist: People begging at traffic lights could have had full lives; everyone contributes either positively or negatively to society.

outline.heading: Neglected youth and our failure
outline.gist: Young people raised amid abuse, addiction and no role models, including Muslim teens already addicted in high school, are failures of the community, not of a 20-year-old.

outline.heading: Corruption weakens the next generation
outline.gist: Bringing war, drugs, prostitution and gambling into a society produces weak families and a weak country that eventually collapses.

outline.heading: The four penalties of hirabah
outline.gist: Execution, crucifixion, amputation of opposite hand and foot, or exile, because the crime threatens public safety and the future of the ummah.

outline.heading: Ask those who have lived through war
outline.gist: Iraqis, Syrians, Yemenis and Palestinians know what war does to families, homes and children's minds.

outline.heading: Fourteen years of war change a people
outline.gist: He avoids returning to Syria to keep his memory of the country before the war; decades of oppression and war have changed its values, and the judge chooses the penalty by the offence.

outline.heading: Rape falls under hirabah
outline.gist: Rape, unlike consensual zina, robs women of safety in public and is treated as terror; the strictness reflects equal care for the public's rights.

outline.heading: Without the collective there is no ummah
outline.gist: Islam rests on the strength of its units, families, communities and countries, and sacrificing them for individual freedom leaves nothing for the future.

outline.heading: The first person to bring drugs to a city
outline.gist: Introducing drugs sends generations in the wrong direction; if that does not feel like a grave crime, we have been numbed.

outline.heading: Private sin versus public sin
outline.gist: Zina is a major sin, but only its public form is punished because it normalizes haram; four witnesses are required and those who spy are themselves punished.

outline.heading: Repentance before capture
outline.gist: Those who reform before they are caught are treated in light of their repentance, because the aim is protecting the community, not brutality.

outline.heading: Cursed by Dawud and Isa for silence
outline.gist: Two prophets of the Children of Israel cursed the disbelievers among them because they did not forbid one another the wrong they committed.

outline.heading: Not wanting to rock the boat
outline.gist: Ignoring an agreed wrong to spare feelings cost them their ethics and their deen, and they continue in loss.

outline.heading: The beer in the masjid
outline.gist: Objecting gently but clearly is how a community protects itself; ignore one man drinking in the masjid and soon the rows will hold cans.

outline.heading: Interlude
Witnesses to a deathbed bequest
outline.gist: Without notaries or records, a dying person's bequest relied on two just witnesses, or two others when travelling.

outline.heading: Held after the prayer to swear
outline.gist: The witnesses must be practising Muslims, kept after salah to swear they will not sell their testimony.

outline.heading: Bribery and replacing sinful witnesses
outline.gist: Large estates invite bribes to change testimony; witnesses later found openly sinful are replaced by others.

outline.heading: Oaths that make witnesses afraid to lie
outline.gist: The replacement witnesses swear their testimony is truer, so that people fear the consequences of a false oath.

outline.heading: Can we trust one another to convey the truth?
outline.gist: From corrupting society to silence about wrong, the third level is the simplest: honest testimony, without which a society has no hope.

outline.heading: The foundation of hadith criticism
outline.gist: This verse became the basis for judging narrators, since the Prophet's life reached us through companions' testimony long before it was widely written down.

outline.heading: The scholar who would not take the hadith
outline.gist: A scholar travelled far to hear a narrator, saw him trick his camel with an empty hand, and left without his hadith; such strictness is why we trust what we narrate.

outline.heading: Outro

6:36.ar: ۞إِنَّمَا يَسۡتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡمَعُونَۘ وَٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ يُرۡجَعُونَ
6:36.en: Only those who hear will respond. But the dead - Allah will resurrect them; then to Him they will be returned

6:37.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦۚ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَادِرٌ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُنَزِّلَ ءَايَةࣰ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
6:37.en: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know

6:38.ar: وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا طَٰٓئِرࣲ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيۡهِ إِلَّآ أُمَمٌ أَمۡثَالُكُمۚ مَّا فَرَّطۡنَا فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يُحۡشَرُونَ
6:38.en: And there is no creature on [or within] the earth or bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered

6:39.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا صُمࣱّ وَبُكۡمࣱ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِۗ مَن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يُضۡلِلۡهُ وَمَن يَشَأۡ يَجۡعَلۡهُ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
6:39.en: But those who deny Our verses are deaf and dumb within darknesses. Whomever Allah wills - He leaves astray; and whomever He wills - He puts him on a straight path

6:83.ar: وَتِلۡكَ حُجَّتُنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتࣲ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
6:83.en: And that was Our [conclusive] argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing

6:84.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ إِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَۚ كُلًّا هَدَيۡنَاۚ وَنُوحًا هَدَيۡنَا مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِۦ دَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيۡمَٰنَ وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُوسُفَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَهَٰرُونَۚ وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
6:84.en: And We gave to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - all [of them] We guided. And Noah, We guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good

6:85.ar: وَزَكَرِيَّا وَيَحۡيَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَإِلۡيَاسَۖ كُلࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
6:85.en: And Zechariah and John and Jesus and Elias - and all were of the righteous

6:86.ar: وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلۡيَسَعَ وَيُونُسَ وَلُوطࣰ اۚ وَكُلࣰّ ا فَضَّلۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
6:86.en: And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot - and all [of them] We preferred over the worlds

6:87.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَابَآئِهِمۡ وَذُرِّيَّٰتِهِمۡ وَإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡۖ وَٱجۡتَبَيۡنَٰهُمۡ وَهَدَيۡنَٰهُمۡ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
6:87.en: And [some] among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers - and We chose them and We guided them to a straight path

6:88.ar: ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهۡدِي بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦۚ وَلَوۡ أَشۡرَكُواْ لَحَبِطَ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
6:88.en: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated others with Allah, then worthless for them would be whatever they were doing

6:89.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحُكۡمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَۚ فَإِن يَكۡفُرۡ بِهَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ فَقَدۡ وَكَّلۡنَا بِهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا لَّيۡسُواْ بِهَا بِكَٰفِرِينَ
6:89.en: Those are the ones to whom We gave the Scripture and authority and prophethood. But if the disbelievers deny it, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not therein disbelievers

6:90.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۖ فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقۡتَدِهۡۗ قُل لَّآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرًاۖ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكۡرَىٰ لِلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
6:90.en: Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for this message no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds

6:141.ar: ۞وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَ جَنَّٰتࣲ مَّعۡرُوشَٰتࣲ وَغَيۡرَ مَعۡرُوشَٰتࣲ وَٱلنَّخۡلَ وَٱلزَّرۡعَ مُخۡتَلِفًا أُكُلُهُۥ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَٰبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهࣲۚ كُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَءَاتُواْ حَقَّهُۥ يَوۡمَ حَصَادِهِۦۖ وَلَا تُسۡرِفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُسۡرِفِينَ
6:141.en: And He it is who causes gardens to grow, [both] trellised and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of different [kinds of] food and olives and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of [each of] its fruit when it yields and give its due [zakah] on the day of its harvest. And be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

7:179.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ذَرَأۡنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِۖ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ أَعۡيُنࣱ لَّا يُبۡصِرُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمۡ ءَاذَانࣱ لَّا يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَآۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ بَلۡ هُمۡ أَضَلُّۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡغَٰفِلُونَ
7:179.en: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless

mwKnx6gkOQo.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 7: Quranic Themes 2 - Pillars of Eman
mwKnx6gkOQo.one_line: Three pillars of eman from Al-An'am: listening to Allah's signs, following the prophets as role models, and turning faith into action.
mwKnx6gkOQo.summary: He opens by rejecting 'belief' as a translation of eman: in the West belief means holding something without evidence, while eman is an acknowledgement of Allah built on evidence gathered over a lifetime and lived out through obedience, affirmed in the heart, spoken and acted upon. Al-An'am, focused on the relationship with Allah, gives him three pillars. First, the ability to truly listen: those who respond are those who hear, while people who have killed off their conscience demand miracles they do not need. Animals and birds are nations like us that hear but cannot reflect, and a person who ignores the signs already around him is no better than livestock. Second, role models: no one finds Allah alone, and the long page naming the prophets ends with the command to follow their guidance, as a worshipper follows the imam. Islam came through twenty-three years of the Prophet living the Quran and through chains of people learning from those who learned before them; replacing that with YouTube and AI chatbots, and neglecting scholars, lets knowledge vanish even with books everywhere. Third, action: Allah's gardens are to be eaten and enjoyed, their zakat paid at harvest, and nothing wasted.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-An'am and the relationship with Allah
outline.gist: The surah, reported to have been revealed at once, focuses on the relationship with Allah; its first half defines eman and its second half shows how to practise it.

outline.heading: Eman is not 'belief'
outline.gist: Belief suggests accepting something without evidence; eman is acknowledging Allah from accumulated evidence and committing to Him through obedience, which is why the Bedouins were told to say they had submitted.

outline.heading: Heart, tongue and limbs
outline.gist: Most scholars define eman as affirmation in the heart, verbal declaration and action.

outline.heading: Interlude
Only those who listen respond
outline.gist: You cannot choose what you hear but you choose whether to listen; the 'dead' are those who have killed off their conscience and reason.

outline.heading: Why no miracle?
outline.gist: Allah could send one, but earlier miracles produced no faith and rejecting one brings punishment.

outline.heading: Animals and birds are nations like you
outline.gist: A verse that seems out of place: every creature is a recorded nation that will be gathered to Allah.

outline.heading: First pillar: learning from the signs
outline.gist: Eman requires the ability to hear, reflect and learn from Allah's signs; inherited faith without it is missing pieces.

outline.heading: Hearing without listening
outline.gist: Animals hear but cannot reflect; a person who witnesses without benefiting is no different from them.

outline.heading: Like livestock, or worse
outline.gist: A parallel verse describes people with hearts, eyes and ears they do not use; they are worse than cattle because cattle have no choice.

outline.heading: You don't need a miracle; it's all there
outline.gist: Allah has presented Himself in all of creation; there are those who listen and those who do not.

outline.heading: Beyond survival: guidance depends on listening
outline.gist: Animals reach only survival conclusions while humans can transcend them; Allah guides or leaves astray according to whether one listens.

outline.heading: Interlude
Second pillar: role models
outline.gist: The mind cannot find God alone; growing up sane requires role models, who themselves needed role models, and ours are the prophets.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's argument and Allah's choice
outline.gist: Allah gave Ibrahim his argument and raises in rank whom He wills; questioning His choice of prophets is disrespectful.

outline.heading: Prophets across time with one message
outline.gist: The named prophets came from different eras and places but brought the same message, with the book, judgment and prophethood.

outline.heading: Different outcomes, same steadfastness
outline.gist: Some prophets were killed, expelled, obeyed or ignored; the Prophet is consoled that his people's rejection is not new.

outline.heading: A people who will never reject it
outline.gist: Allah has entrusted the message to others who will carry it, so the Prophet need not be troubled by those who refuse.

outline.heading: 'Follow their guidance': what a role model means
outline.gist: The command means taking them as a model, exactly as one follows the imam in prayer whether one likes him or not.

outline.heading: Islam came through a life, not a book in the desert
outline.gist: The Quran came with twenty-three years of the Prophet living it; without him no one could make sense of it, and we should feel how fortunate we are to have him.

outline.heading: The chain of people learning from people
outline.gist: The companions filled their eyes and ears with the Prophet, the next generations with them, and the Prophet himself learned from earlier prophets.

outline.heading: Learning Islam from YouTube and chatbots
outline.gist: People now take religion from screens and AI rather than from teachers, and the value of scholarship has been downgraded.

outline.heading: Knowledge disappears with the scholars
outline.gist: Allah removes knowledge by taking the scholars, not by erasing books; each scholar who dies without students is a lost link.

outline.heading: Prophets ask for no payment
outline.gist: The prophets sought no wage, only to teach, which is what the message is built on.

outline.heading: Third pillar: eat, pay its due, do not waste
outline.gist: Allah's varied gardens are for eating and enjoying, but zakat is due at harvest and waste is disliked; eman must become behaviour.

Turn faith into action: enjoy what Allah provides, pay its zakat and do not waste.

4:65.ar: فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَرَجࣰ ا مِّمَّا قَضَيۡتَ وَيُسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمࣰ ا
4:65.en: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission

4:71.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ خُذُواْ حِذۡرَكُمۡ فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنفِرُواْ جَمِيعࣰ ا
4:71.en: O you who have believed, take your precaution and [either] go forth in companies or go forth all together

4:72.ar: وَإِنَّ مِنكُمۡ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ فَإِنۡ أَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالَ قَدۡ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِذۡ لَمۡ أَكُن مَّعَهُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:72.en: And indeed, there is among you he who lingers behind; and if disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has favored me in that I was not present with them

4:73.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَصَٰبَكُمۡ فَضۡلࣱ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَن لَّمۡ تَكُنۢ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ مَوَدَّةࣱ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي كُنتُ مَعَهُمۡ فَأَفُوزَ فَوۡزًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:73.en: But if bounty comes to you from Allah, he will surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection. "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment

4:160.ar: فَبِظُلۡمࣲ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ طَيِّبَٰتٍ أُحِلَّتۡ لَهُمۡ وَبِصَدِّهِمۡ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:160.en: For wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We made unlawful for them [certain] good foods which had been lawful to them, and for their averting from the way of Allah many [people]

4:161.ar: وَأَخۡذِهِمُ ٱلرِّبَوٰاْ وَقَدۡ نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ وَأَكۡلِهِمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِۚ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ مِنۡهُمۡ عَذَابًا أَلِيمࣰ ا
4:161.en: And [for] their taking of usury while they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the people's wealth unjustly. And we have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment

4:162.ar: لَّٰكِنِ ٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَٱلۡمُقِيمِينَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ سَنُؤۡتِيهِمۡ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمًا
4:162.en: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. And the establishers of prayer [especially] and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: [Fasting for] a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] - then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. But to fast is best for you, if you only knew

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error

3:75.ar: ۞وَمِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِقِنطَارࣲ يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ إِن تَأۡمَنۡهُ بِدِينَارࣲ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيۡكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ قَآئِمࣰ اۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡنَا فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلࣱ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡكَذِبَ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
3:75.en: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount [of wealth], he will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a [single] silver coin, he will not return it to you unless you are constantly standing over him [demanding it]. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlearned." And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it]
